title: Scheduled jobs with timers in Node
when: A Node process must run a task every few minutes, daily at a set time, or retry later, without an external scheduler.
prompt:
Goal: Jobs that fire at the right wall clock time, never overlap, survive errors and log every run.
Steps:
1. Fixed intervals: chain setTimeout after each run completes instead of setInterval, so slow runs cannot overlap.
2. Daily at 03:00: compute the delay to the next local occurrence, schedule it, and recompute after each run (absorbs daylight saving shifts).
3. setTimeout caps near 24.8 days; for longer waits re-check hourly.
4. Wrap each run in try and catch; log start, end, duration and errors; save lastRun to a small state file so a restart can catch up a missed daily run.
5. Add a few seconds of jitter when jobs share a minute, and keep a running flag per job.
6. unref() helper timers; clear all timers on SIGINT and SIGTERM.
Quality bar:
- A failing job logs and runs again at its next slot.
- Times are logged in ISO format with offset.
- Schedules are configured by name and time.
Pitfalls:
- setInterval drift and overlap on slow jobs.
- Adding 86400000 ms for tomorrow, wrong on daylight saving days.
- Silently losing scheduled work on restart.
Verify:
- [ ] No setInterval for long jobs.
- [ ] Next run recomputed after each run.
- [ ] Each run inside try and catch.
- [ ] Signals clear timers.
Output: scheduler.mjs with schedule(name, rule, fn) and jobs/*.mjs for each task.

examples.input: rodar um backup todo dia às 3 da manhã
examples.output: scheduler.mjs computing the next 03:00, try/catch per run, lastRun catch-up after restart
